text: This capstone used every chapter that came before it. Chapter 1 is why parsing a Sentinel incident and calling a REST API with proper pagination needed no re-introduction when Lesson 29's polling function needed writing. Chapter 2 is why reaching into Microsoft Graph and scripting against Sentinel's own API felt ordinary rather than new.

Chapter 3 is the backbone of the whole pipeline: Lesson 9's line between what SOAR automates and what it doesn't, Lesson 11's enrich-before-a-human-looks pattern, and Lesson 12's containment-needs-an-approval-gate lesson, which execute_containment turned into actual code. Chapter 4's threat-intel scoring is what keeps that enrichment from becoming noise of its own.

Chapter 5 is why the pipeline posts a proposed action to an approval channel before executing it, and tracks processed incident IDs so re-running the loop never re-contains the same finding twice -- ChatOps and idempotency, applied to a live pipeline instead of a standalone example.

Chapter 6 is exactly what made Lesson 30 possible: pip-audit and bandit as real scanning tools, and Lesson 24's hard-won argument that a gate should fail the build on Critical and High findings only. Chapter 7 is why that gate matters for this repository specifically -- a script holding live credentials is exactly the target Lesson 25 and Lesson 26 were written for.

Lesson 31's Caldera Finance case study isn't a separate topic -- it's the same material from the failure side. Bramwell's script defaults to dry-run and refuses to run without approval; Caldera's had neither, and one overbroad query turned one compromise into thirty-nine lockouts. The guardrails exist because correlation logic will sometimes be wrong.

Python Security Automation, SOAR and DevSecOps is complete: seven chapters of fundamentals, APIs, SOAR, threat intel, orchestration, and pipeline security, proven on one real gated pipeline, one real CI/CD gate, and a case study of what happens without either. Next in this path: Zero Trust and Enterprise Security Capstone, closing the Advanced Specialization stage.
